### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**7** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json da6f0ce35da60bf81e79890b227815a989f9b165` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `39f9768f4971b29ce015860c8a7b5dd134e16172` — the merge of head `f3768a460e0ea970462b374dc23b592c7dc8f63c` into base `da6f0ce35da60bf81e79890b227815a989f9b165`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 39f9768f4971b29ce015860c8a7b5dd134e16172 && git checkout 39f9768f4971b29ce015860c8a7b5dd134e16172
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin da6f0ce35da60bf81e79890b227815a989f9b165 f3768a460e0ea970462b374dc23b592c7dc8f63c && git checkout -B drift-repro da6f0ce35da60bf81e79890b227815a989f9b165 && git merge --no-ff f3768a460e0ea970462b374dc23b592c7dc8f63c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json da6f0ce35da60bf81e79890b227815a989f9b165
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `f3768a460e0ea970462b374dc23b592c7dc8f63c`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #28657 (its body and all 3 comments: triage, claim, os-dev-report 6559402196), PR #28708 (body, 5 files, net diff against merge-base `e4ec4f22c5`), and the 48 latest check-runs on the head. Every check-run is `success` or a path-filtered `skipped` (UI, docs, opt-in harnesses; the diff touches no `ui/**` and no docs). Test Core 1-8/8, Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate and Governed Surface Queue Guard are all green.

### ① Derived judgments

The accept-set change: on the REST `/actions` door and the MCP `run_action` bridge, a same-origin `type:'api'` action whose caller-scope subject load was denied used to answer 404 `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`. It now forwards and answers its target's answer, when the declaration needs no field of the row. The forward-refusal relay also reads a target's string `error`. The widening is judged **right**, point by point.

- **(a) No unreadable row field reaches the request: holds, twice over.**
  - `buildApiActionRequest` (`action-execution.ts:1313`) reads the row in exactly two places: the `{field}` path substitution (`:1341`) and the `recordIdParam` / `recordIdField` seed (`:1387`).
  - The `${...}` scopes are `param` and `ctx` only (`:1221`). `ctx.recordId` is the routed id. Every substituted value goes through `encodeURIComponent`, so a param cannot inject a `{field}` token into the path.
  - The `outputs.*` fold (`:1376`) reads params. `bodyExtra` (`:1420`) reads the declaration. `organizationId` reads `ec`.
  - `apiActionRequestReadsSubjectRow` (`:3434`) puts exactly those two row reads ahead of the forward. It applies the same regex as the builder to the raw `target`, and it errs toward the 404: `{ID}` and a bare `${x}` both count as row reads.
  - Independently, `apiForwardSubjectRecord` (`:3454`) hands the builder `{ id: recordId }` and nothing else on a denied load. By construction, the leftover row on a denied load was already only the stamped `{ id }` (`loadActionSubjectRecord`, `:3295`), so the second guard is defence in depth, not the only line.
  - Both doors use it: REST at `domains/actions.ts:915`, MCP at `action-execution.ts:3999`.
  - Pinned for both doors by the `{email}` path case and the `recordIdField: 'email'` case (404, nothing forwarded), with a firing control on a readable row and the helper table.
- **(b) The 404 holds on every other branch, at both doors.**
  - `forwardsOnDeniedSubjectLoad` (`:3416`) is false for a declarative update (it reads `operation` before `type`), for `flow`, for `script`/body and for an off-origin `api` action. In each of those cases `refuseDeniedSubjectLoadBeforeDispatch` is `refuseDeniedSubjectLoad` unchanged.
  - The declarative update also runs ahead of the call at both doors and keeps its own `refuseDeniedSubjectLoad` (`:3676`).
  - The REST `actionType` is `actionDef.type` when it is a string (`actions.ts:689`), so the forward predicate and the `actionType === 'api'` branch (`:903`) cannot disagree. Every arm of that branch returns, so a skipped refusal can never fall through to the trusted `actionContext`. The same holds at MCP (`:3986`).
  - The existing `[#16370]` flow and script/body pins and the ROW-SCOPED flow pin are green in Test Core.
- **(c) The forward opens nothing beyond a direct call with the same credential.**
  - `forwardApiAction` (`:1810`) carries only the allow-listed caller headers.
  - The mark header (`:1849`) carries no trust. Its only readers are the loop refusal and the audit hint, and `action-invocation-audit.ts:25` says so.
  - No system or elevated context is built on the api branch. It sits ahead of `actionContext`, `buildActionEngineFacade` and `buildActionExecutionContext`.
  - `apiForwardCredentialRefusal` and the scope-family rule run unchanged.
  - One non-blocking observation: an OAuth agent at a platform target is carried by the ADR-0090 D10 rule 5 minted credential, which resolves to the same agent principal. That path existed before this PR and is unchanged by it. The approval actions are not `ai.exposed`, so no agent reaches them.
  - Existence: a filtered row and an absent id still collapse into one answer at the door. Whatever the target answers, it would answer the same to a direct call.
- **(d) Reach: right.**
  - Only the REST `/actions` door and MCP `run_action` call the new function (`actions.ts:888`, `action-execution.ts:3977`).
  - `resume_run` (`domains/mcp.ts:1200`) and the declarative executor keep `refuseDeniedSubjectLoad`.
  - The new helpers are not re-exported from `packages/runtime/src/index.ts`, so the published type surface is unchanged.
  - The rule is generic, not approvals-only. That matches the claim's declared Clause-② on the card ("a same-origin api action on a caller-denied subject row answers its target's answer"), and it follows ADR-0066 D4: the target authorizes the caller itself.
  - `pending-approver-read-grant.ts`, the member grant on `sys_approval_request`, `packages/spec/**` and `ui/**` are untouched, as the triage ruled.
- **Relay (`:1991`): right.** A target's string `error` is now read before the "its target answered HTTP N" fallback. The sentence is the target's own answer to this caller, so it discloses nothing a direct call would not. This was the card's same-path ride-along. It is pinned on both doors, for the 400 case and the 403 case.
- **Card pin owed: met.** `packages/verify/src/action-door-api-forward-denied-subject.test.ts` boots the real stack: real dispatcher, real approvals routes, real in-process forward, no doubled fetch. A non-admin pending approver approves through the action door, and the request moves. A stranger gets the route's own 403. Test Core is green on this head.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/28657-api-action-forward-denied-subject.md` declares `@objectstack/runtime: patch`. The diff publishes only runtime `dist`; `@objectstack/verify` gains a test file only. `Metadata-protocol: none` and a non-protocol widening each mean `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3). **Right.**
- `Clause-②: yes (widening: ...)` appears line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset, and matches the accept-set change judged in ①. Nothing is narrowed, so there is no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0]** (the approval actions are not `ai.exposed`; the `run_action` parity is pinned on an exposed object): **answered A, leave them unexposed.**
  - Exposing decision actions to agents is a plugin-approvals product decision outside this card.
  - Base and head refuse them at the same exposure gate, so nothing regresses.
  - The MCP parity this card owes is the door's rule, and that is pinned on the identical declaration shape.
  - No card is opened from this review. If the product wants agent decisions, that is a separate plugin-approvals card.
- **out_of_scope_findings[0]** (the approvals routes answer `{ code, error }`, not the ADR-0112 envelope): accepted as noted, not filed. It is pre-existing, and this head only reads that sentence at the forward. It is no must-fix here.
- **dogfood_battery n/a**: right. The title has no `!` and the change has no `(narrowing)` arm.
- **mcp_calls 0 / api_writes 2**: consistent with the inputs read.
- No other dev flag is raised.

No must-fix findings.
